title: Turtle workshop for advanced coders
instruction: Draw the target with the shortest possible program. Every command counts, including repeat, learn and calling a procedure. You get a star if you stay within the limit.

levels.hint: The inner angle of a triangle is 60°. But the turtle doesn’t turn by the inner angle; it turns by how much it changes direction.
levels.why: Over the whole trip round, the turtle turns by 360°. Three turns: 360 / 3 = 120°. With a 60° turn, it would draw part of a hexagon.

levels.goal: A five-pointed star in one stroke, side 150.
levels.hint: When drawing a star, the turtle goes round the centre twice. How many degrees is that in total?
levels.why: Two trips round are 720°. 720 / 5 = 144°. For a pentagon, 72° would be enough. The bigger turn sends the turtle across the centre, and that’s why the lines cross.

levels.goal: A rosette: 12 squares with side 80, each turned by 30° around the same corner.
levels.hint: Draw one square with a loop. Then wrap the whole square, turn included, in another loop.
levels.why: A nested loop: the inner one draws the square, the outer one turns it. 12 × 30° = 360°, so the rosette closes up. Without loops, it would be 108 commands.

levels.goal: Three squares with a shared corner: sides 30, 60 and 90.
levels.target: nauč ctverec :s [ opakuj 4 [ dopředu :s vpravo 90 ] ] ctverec 30 ctverec 60 ctverec 90
levels.hint: Teach the turtle a new command square, and pass it the side length as the parameter :s.
levels.why: A procedure is a new command, and a parameter is a variable that has a different value each time it is called. After four turns, the square returns to its corner, and that’s why the next one starts in the same place.

levels.goal: A row of five squares with side 20 next to each other, gaps of 10, with no connecting lines.
levels.target: nauč ctverec :s [ opakuj 4 [ dopředu :s vpravo 90 ] ] opakuj 5 [ ctverec 20 pero nahoru vpravo 90 dopředu 30 vlevo 90 pero dolů ]
levels.hint: After each square, the turtle must move right without drawing, and then turn back up again.
levels.why: The turtle holds a state: position, direction and pen. After moving, it must restore the state (left 90, pen down), or the next square would be turned or invisible. A step of 30 is the side of 20 plus the gap of 10.

debrief: A loop saves commands, a nested loop multiplies them, and a procedure with a parameter turns one shape into a whole family. All the while, the turtle holds its state: where it is, which way it faces and whether it’s drawing. Just like the variables in your program.
